      "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact. The antecedent is FALSE at its only intended witness. Satisfiability elsewhere is exactly what makes that invisible.\n\nWORSE: my own project already had the refutation. Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean exists to record this as 'trap (c): a P -> Q whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting', with the general theorems to check it -- and I had imported nothing from it. The strengthening was FROM a weak condition my own file proved holds at the curve TO one my own project proved fails at the Picard scheme.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE RULE. When you replace a hypothesis H by a 'more standard' H', H' => H is not enough -- that direction is what makes the substitution LOOK conservative. Ask what H' implies that H does not (here: quasi-compactness), then check that consequence at the intended witness. And grep your own tree for a file whose title is a negation ('NotProper', 'NoGo', 'Refute') before publishing a strengthening: the counterexample is often already landed one import away.\n\nALSO: the weakened repair is where tautologies hide. My first repair -- 'every finite set that lies in a good open lies in an affine open' -- is PROVABLE for every scheme with its hypothesis unused. Elaborate the candidate weakening with the binder discarded before shipping it (pic-g filed the same shape as I-1660 the same day).",

      "body": "AN 'ONLY PRODUCER IS FIELD-ONLY' CLAIM IS A CENSUS OF THE NAME YOU GUESSED, AND THE RING-LEVEL VERSION IS OFTEN LANDED UNDER A DIFFERENT MAP.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g 0096 r6, refuted by a fresh-context audit of my own file). I published that the picEtAffineEquiv/unit presentation seam has exactly one general producer -- PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section -- that it is stated over a FIELD and needs a curve section there, and that ring-level surjectivity of PicEtAff.unit is therefore the honest next brick. Every clause was checkable and the conclusion was false: picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:161) supplies the same seam at an ARBITRARY test RING, no field, no section, no curve binder, with 11 call sites.\n\nWHY MY CENSUS MISSED IT, and this is the reusable part. I searched for producers of the SEAM'S NAME -- surjectivity of  -- because that is the shape of the conclusion I wanted. The landed producer is not about 's surjectivity at all: it is an AFFINE-CONSISTENCY lemma for a DIFFERENT map (relPicToPicEt) which happens to have the seam as its conclusion. A grep for 'unit_surjective' finds it never; a search for the CONCLUSION 'picEtAffineEquiv _ = PicEtAff.unit _ _' finds it first.\n\nSO THE RULE: when you are about to write 'the only producer is X, and X is too strong', search for the CONCLUSION you need, not for the strengthened statement whose name you have. The name census answers 'who proved this lemma'; the obligation is 'who lands this Prop', and a lemma about another map can land it while carrying none of the binders you were about to price.\n\nAND THE SECOND-ORDER COST, which is why this is worth a memory item rather than a header note: the false claim RELOCATED THE GAP. I named ring-level surjectivity of  as the next brick; the actually-open statement is surjectivity of relPicToPicEt onto picEt -- a different map, different proof, and one the tree already treats as a real condition (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199 calls membership in its range 'honesty'). A misidentified next brick sends the next lane to build something nobody needs.",

      "body": "A \"TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X\" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: \"going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured\". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.\n\nIt is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.\n\nTHE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing \"route X does not work\", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.\n\nWHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.\n\nCOROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check.",

      "body": "A LOCALISATION REDUCTION IS EMPTIED BY THE CONSUMER OWN OUTER QUANTIFIER, AND EVERY PER-STATEMENT CHECK PASSES.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, AJCR 0096 r7, Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean; audit I-1657/I-1660, reproduced by me).\n\nWHAT HAPPENED. I reduced an obligation P(A) at an arbitrary test algebra to a pointwise-local form: for every prime p of A, some f outside p with P(Localization.Away f). At a FIXED A that is a real reduction with no route back, and I verified it. I then composed it over all A into two producers of the goal object -- and those hypotheses are LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT to the global ones they were meant to weaken, because Localization.Away f is ITSELF a test algebra, so the consumer own forall-A already ranges over it. The converse is one line with the trivial witness f = 1.\n\nWHY EVERY CHECK PASSED. Sorry-free, axiom-clean against a sorryAx control, rooted, build green, non-vacuous (both hypotheses used, linter clean), and the fixed-A lemma genuinely is a reduction. Nothing local to any statement is wrong. The defect is the INTERACTION between my inner quantifier and the consumer outer one, and no per-statement check can see it.\n\nTHE TEST, and it costs one probe: before pricing a localisation, pointwise, or restriction reduction as progress, PROVE THE CONVERSE WITH THE TRIVIAL WITNESS -- f = 1, the identity localisation, V = top, the whole space. If it closes, the reduction only helps at a FIXED base object, and you must then check whether the consumer has that shape. Mine did not.\n\nSECOND, SMALLER TRAP FROM THE SAME FILE: my \"local ring\" interface was about Localization.Away f, which is a BASIC OPEN and not a local ring (IsLocalRing fails to synthesize). A lane with a genuinely local computation holds Localization.AtPrime, and the AtPrime-to-Away bridge is spreading out -- ask which one your consumer actually has before naming the interface.\n\nSibling of \"substitute the trivial value in layer one\" and \"free factor vs localisation\".",

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

          "body": "RIDER, and it nearly caused a second bogus repair. Verify board prose by PARSING the summary field, never by grepping the file.\n\nAfter a roadmap set --pin-commit write I grepped for my newly appended section and got 0 hits, concluded the CLI had clobbered me again, and started re-appending. The grep was wrong, not the CLI: yaml.safe_dump wraps at 88 columns, so any phrase longer than a few words spans lines and no grep can match it. python3 -c \"yaml.safe_load(...)[\\\"summary\\\"]\" then showed all five distinctive phrases present, 14685 chars, three pins, owner cleared.\n\nSo the original rule (check the commit STAT) stands, and this is its companion: a zero grep hit on board prose is evidence about line wrapping, not about content. Both halves matter -- the stat catches real loss, and parsing prevents inventing loss that did not happen."

      "body": "A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.\n\nNO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.\n\nTHE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.\n\nTHE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.\n\nCOROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].",

      "body": "VANISHING-VOCABULARY SPELLINGS ARE ONE ANTECEDENT -- and the commit that ships the 'reduced' producer often ships the iff that proves it is a re-spelling.\n\nAJC DivFamilyZero.lean, AJC.picrep.divzero, pic-e runs 0095->0105. Over three rounds the same lane landed three producers of Div0-representable, each 'reducing' the obligation to a fresh vocabulary:\n  _of_isZero               : IsZero x.F\n  _of_forall_subsingleton_sections : forall V, Subsingleton Gamma(x.F,V)\n  _of_forall_isEmpty_schematicSupport : IsEmpty(schematicSupport x.F)\nEach docstring bills its antecedent as 'the sharpest/purest/most-geometric honest form.' At every DivFamily x.F is quasicoherent, and the file itself ships isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections and isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport -- so the three antecedents are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (all = IsZero x.F). None is weaker. The obligation HasFiberDeg 0 -> IsZero x.F is untouched; only the vocabulary on its RHS rotates.\n\nTHE TELL, sharper than I-1622: when a 'reduction' commit also lands an IFF between the new antecedent and the old one, the iff IS the proof that no reduction happened. Emptiness-of-support, subsingleton-sections, and IsZero are one node with three names; a producer parameterised on any of them is the same producer. Before crediting 'reduced to X', rw the shipped iffs and check whether the new antecedent closes the old goal with no hypotheses -- if it does, it is coordinates, not distance. The real distance for divzero lives in DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean (carrier bridge + degree-0=>empty-fibre), which no spelling of the RHS moves.",

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneLocus
     7	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Restrict
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The universal divisor rank-one open contract
    11	
    12	The genus divisor representer is unconditional, while the rank-one restriction still needs a
    13	family-level open-locus producer.  This file separates those two facts.  The predicate below is
    14	the inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` along the represented universal Abel map.  A
    15	`DivRankOneOpenData` witness identifies that predicate with the range of one actual open of the
    16	representer; only after that witness is supplied do we define the open subscheme.
    17	
    18	This shape prevents a logical `Subfunctor` from being silently reinterpreted as a scheme.  It also
    19	gives the canonical inverse lane a stable contract: it consumes the witness equality and can use
    20	the resulting open inclusion and all of its pullbacks without choosing a generator.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    25	
    26	universe u
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    29	
    30	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    33	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    34	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    35	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    36	
    37	noncomputable section
    38	
    39	/-- The universal genus-divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/
    40	def divRankOneUniversalPredicate :
    41	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
    42	  divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi
    43	
    44	/-- The Yoneda map induced by the inclusion of an open of an object in the slice.  Naming this
    45	map is useful to consumers which need the actual factorisation through the open, rather than only
    46	the proposition that a point lies in its range. -/
    47	def openSubfunctorMap (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
    48	    yoneda.obj (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) ⟶ yoneda.obj D :=
    49	  yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) U.ι)
    50	
    51	/-- The subfunctor represented by an open `U` of an object `D` in the slice over `Spec k`.
    52	
    53	Its values are precisely morphisms which factor through the open immersion `U.ι`; using the
    54	Yoneda range keeps this definition independent of any chosen affine presentation of `U`. -/
    55	def openSubfunctor (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
    56	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj D) :=
    57	  Subfunctor.range (openSubfunctorMap D U)
    58	
    59	/-- Unpack range membership into the actual source point and its equality in the ambient Yoneda
    60	functor.  This is the pointwise factorisation API used by inverse constructions. -/
    61	theorem openSubfunctor_mem_iff
    62	    (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens)
    63	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    64	    (x : (yoneda.obj D).obj T) :
    65	    x ∈ (openSubfunctor D U).obj T ↔
    66	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom))).obj T,
    67	        (openSubfunctorMap D U).app T y = x := by
    68	  rfl
    69	
    70	/-- An explicit geometric certificate for the universal rank-one predicate.
    71	
    72	The equality is the missing family-level producer/gluing statement: it identifies the logical
    73	preimage with an actual open of the canonical genus representer.  No default or top-open witness
    74	is manufactured here. -/
    75	structure DivRankOneOpenData (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi] where
    76	  carrier : (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens
    77	  carrier_eq :
    78	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) carrier =
    79	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi
    80	
    81	/-- The open subscheme supplied by a `DivRankOneOpenData` witness. -/
    82	def DivRankOneOpen (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) : Scheme :=
    83	  h.carrier.toScheme
    84	
    85	/-- The canonical open immersion into the genus divisor representer. -/
    86	def divRankOneOpenMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    87	    DivRankOneOpen pi h ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
    88	  h.carrier.ι
    89	
    90	theorem divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion
    91	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    92	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenMap pi h) := by
    93	  change IsOpenImmersion h.carrier.ι
    94	  infer_instance
    95	
    96	/-- The open represented object, retained in the slice over `Spec k` for consumers of the affine
    97	divisor functor. -/
    98	def divRankOneOpenOver (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    99	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   100	  Over.mk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)
   101	
   102	/-- The inclusion of the certified open, as a morphism in the slice over `Spec k`.
   103	
   104	This is the map whose Yoneda action is consumed by the canonical rank-one Abel inverse.  Naming
   105	it separately keeps consumers independent of the implementation spelling of `divRankOneOpenOver`.
   106	-/
   107	def divRankOneOpenOverMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   108	    divRankOneOpenOver pi h ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C :=
   109	  Over.homMk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h)
   110	
   111	/-- Pull back the certified rank-one open along an arbitrary slice morphism. -/
   112	def divRankOneOpenPullback
   113	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   114	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) : T.left.Opens :=
   115	  q.left ⁻¹ᵁ h.carrier
   116	
   117	theorem divRankOneOpenPullback_isOpenImmersion
   118	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   119	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
   120	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q).ι := by
   121	  infer_instance
   122	
   123	/-- Pointwise form of arbitrary base-change compatibility for the certified open. -/
   124	theorem mem_divRankOneOpenPullback_iff
   125	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   126	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C)
   127	    (x : T.left) :
   128	    x ∈ divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q ↔ q.left.base x ∈ h.carrier := by
   129	  rfl
   130	
   131	/-- The universal predicate is exactly the represented preimage used by the Abel restriction. -/
   132	theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_eq_preimage :
   133	    divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi = divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi :=
   134	  rfl
   135	
   136	/-- The certified open carrier has the universal rank-one predicate as its Yoneda range. -/
   137	theorem divRankOneOpen_carrier_eq
   138	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   139	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier =
   140	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi :=
   141	  h.carrier_eq
   142	
   143	/-- Pointwise form of the witness equality, exposing the exact contract consumed by an inverse.
   144	
   145	The right-hand side is the range of the open immersion, so a consumer can use this theorem to
   146	replace a rank-one predicate proof by a factorisation through `DivRankOneOpen pi h`. -/
   147	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff
   148	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   149	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   150	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   151	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   152	      x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T := by
   153	  rw [h.carrier_eq]
   154	
   155	/-- A point of the universal rank-one predicate factors through the certified open immersion.
   156	
   157	Unlike a bare range-membership proof, the conclusion exposes the source point and the equality
   158	of its image with the given divisor point, which is the exact data needed by a canonical inverse. -/
   159	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization
   160	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   161	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   162	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   163	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   164	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (Over.mk
   165	          (h.carrier.ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom))).obj T,
   166	        (openSubfunctorMap (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).app T y = x := by
   167	  rw [divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x, openSubfunctor_mem_iff]
   168	
   169	/-- The same factorisation contract with the named open object and slice inclusion.
   170	
   171	The source in the preceding theorem is definitionally the slice object
   172	`divRankOneOpenOver pi h`; this corollary gives the stable public names expected by inverse
   173	consumers. -/
   174	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization_over
   175	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   176	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   177	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   178	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   179	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (divRankOneOpenOver pi h)).obj T,
   180	        (yoneda.map (divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h)).app T y = x := by
   181	  rw [divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization pi h x]
   182	  rfl
   183	
   184	/-- A point in the certified open carrier is a point of the universal rank-one predicate. -/
   185	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_of_carrier
   186	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   187	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   188	    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
   189	    (hx : x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T) :
   190	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T := by
   191	  exact (divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x).mpr hx
   192	
   193	/- The logical rank-one predicate remains stable under arbitrary pullback, independently of the
   194	   geometric witness used to represent it by an open. -/
   195	theorem divRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem
   196	    {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   197	    (f : T ⟶ T')
   198	    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
   199	    (hx : x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T) :
   200	    (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).map f x ∈
   201	      (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T' :=
   202	  (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).map f hx
   203	
   204	end
   205	
   206	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!
    10	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    11	
    12	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    13	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    14	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    15	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    16	
    17	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    18	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    19	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
    21	the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    41	
    42	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    43	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    44	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    45	def PicRankOneOpen :
    46	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    47	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    48	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    49	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    50	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    51	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    52	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    53	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    54	      apply Subtype.ext

    64	is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
    65	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/

    67	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    68	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=

    70	    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    71	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    72	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))
    73	
    74	/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
    75	Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
    76	field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
    77	contract. -/
    78	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    79	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
    80	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
    81	      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    82	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    83	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    84	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam)) := by

    88	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations
    89	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    90	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    91	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    92	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    93	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    94	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :

    98	/-- Constructor using the named arbitrary-affine producer predicate. -/
    99	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentationCondition

   101	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   102	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition pi lam) :

   106	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
   107	def picRankOneOpenIncl :

   109	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι

   111	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.

   113	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
   114	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
   115	relative-open gate below. -/
   116	def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
   117	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
   118	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
   119	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   120	
   121	/-- Relative openness of the public locus, in Mathlib's presheaf sense.
   122	
   123	This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
   124	producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is
   125	silently treated as an open subscheme. -/

   137	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
   138	    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
   139	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   140	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))
   141	    (fst : yoneda.obj Z ⟶

   143	    (snd : Z ⟶ X)
   144	    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :
   145	    IsOpenImmersion snd :=

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneLocus
+import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Restrict

+/-!
+# The universal divisor rank-one open contract
+
+The genus divisor representer is unconditional, while the rank-one restriction still needs a
+family-level open-locus producer.  This file separates those two facts.  The predicate below is
+the inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` along the represented universal Abel map.  A
+`DivRankOneOpenData` witness identifies that predicate with the range of one actual open of the
+representer; only after that witness is supplied do we define the open subscheme.
+
+This shape prevents a logical `Subfunctor` from being silently reinterpreted as a scheme.  It also
+gives the canonical inverse lane a stable contract: it consumes the witness equality and can use
+the resulting open inclusion and all of its pullbacks without choosing a generator.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
+
+universe u
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry
+
+variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
+variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
+  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
+variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- The universal genus-divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/
+def divRankOneUniversalPredicate :
+    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
+  divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi
+
+/-- The subfunctor represented by an open `U` of an object `D` in the slice over `Spec k`.
+
+Its values are precisely morphisms which factor through the open immersion `U.ι`; using the
+Yoneda range keeps this definition independent of any chosen affine presentation of `U`. -/
+def openSubfunctor (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
+    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj D) :=
+  Subfunctor.range (yoneda.map
+    (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) U.ι))
+
+/-- An explicit geometric certificate for the universal rank-one predicate.
+
+The equality is the missing family-level producer/gluing statement: it identifies the logical
+preimage with an actual open of the canonical genus representer.  No default or top-open witness
+is manufactured here. -/
+structure DivRankOneOpenData (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi] where
+  carrier : (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens
+  carrier_eq :
+    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) carrier =
+      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi
+
+/-- The open subscheme supplied by a `DivRankOneOpenData` witness. -/
+def DivRankOneOpen (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) : Scheme :=
+  h.carrier.toScheme
+
+/-- The canonical open immersion into the genus divisor representer. -/
+def divRankOneOpenMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
+    DivRankOneOpen pi h ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
+  h.carrier.ι
+
+theorem divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion
+    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
+    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenMap pi h) := by
+  change IsOpenImmersion h.carrier.ι
+  infer_instance
+
+/-- The open represented object, retained in the slice over `Spec k` for consumers of the affine
+divisor functor. -/
+def divRankOneOpenOver (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
+    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
+  Over.mk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)
+
+/-- Pull back the certified rank-one open along an arbitrary slice morphism. -/
+def divRankOneOpenPullback
+    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
+    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) : T.left.Opens :=
+  q.left ⁻¹ᵁ h.carrier
+
+theorem divRankOneOpenPullback_isOpenImmersion
+    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
+    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
+    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q).ι := by
+  infer_instance
+
+/-- Pointwise form of arbitrary base-change compatibility for the certified open. -/
+theorem mem_divRankOneOpenPullback_iff
+    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
+    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C)
+    (x : T.left) :
+    x ∈ divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q ↔ q.left.base x ∈ h.carrier := by
+  rfl
+
+/-- The universal predicate is exactly the represented preimage used by the Abel restriction. -/
+theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_eq_preimage :
+    divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi = divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi :=
+  rfl
+
+/-- The certified open carrier has the universal rank-one predicate as its Yoneda range. -/
+theorem divRankOneOpen_carrier_eq
+    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
+    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier =
+      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi :=
+  h.carrier_eq
+
+/-- Pointwise form of the witness equality, exposing the exact contract consumed by an inverse.
+
+The right-hand side is the range of the open immersion, so a consumer can use this theorem to
+replace a rank-one predicate proof by a factorisation through `DivRankOneOpen pi h`. -/
+theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff
+    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
+    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
+    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
+    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
+      x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T := by
+  rw [h.carrier_eq]
+
+/-- A point in the certified open carrier is a point of the universal rank-one predicate. -/
+theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_of_carrier
+    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
+    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
+    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
+    (hx : x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T) :
+    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T := by
+  exact (divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x).mpr hx
+
+/- The logical rank-one predicate remains stable under arbitrary pullback, independently of the
+   geometric witness used to represent it by an open. -/
+theorem divRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem
+    {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
+    (f : T ⟶ T')
+    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
+    (hx : x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T) :
+    (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).map f x ∈
+      (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T' :=
+  (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).map f hx
+
+end
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# C9b: what `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` of a chart map actually asks for
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` — the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that
    12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes — and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap
    13	row, prices it as **one** obligation: the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 plus the classifier,
    14	CERT-Σ-gated.
    15	
    16	**That pricing is wrong, and this file is the correction.**  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is
    17	`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and
    18	`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:
    19	
    20	1. **relative representability** — for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ 𝓟`, the
    21	   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;
    22	2. **the property clause** — every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.
    23	
    24	The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single
    25	point, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which
    26	is a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on
    27	CERT-Σ for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with
    28	no divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.
    29	
    30	## What this file provides, and what it deliberately does not
    31	
    32	Everything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves
    33	`f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V ⊆ X`.  No `divRep`
    34	endpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `θ` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That
    35	is the point: `IsChartUniv` becomes *this criterion instantiated at* `abelSigmaChart`, and
    36	the divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.
    37	
    38	The criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf — a fibrewise
    39	injectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open — because that is what
    40	mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf
    41	category's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).
    42	
    43	## Main declarations
    44	
    45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` — the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test
    46	  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points
    47	  with the chart points hitting `g`.  This is the *shape* of a fibre-product presentation,
    48	  named so that a producer knows exactly what it owes.
    49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` — **the criterion**:
    50	  a `ChartFibrePresented` datum gives `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, discharging BOTH clauses
    51	  at once.  Certificate-free and divRep-free.
    52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the converse direction that makes
    53	  the split honest: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` *implies* `f` is a monomorphism.  So "the
    54	  Abel map is not a monomorphism", which three files cite as the reason the unrestricted
    55	  certificate fails, is a consequence of the criterion rather than an extra obligation — and
    56	  it shows the elementwise injectivity clause below is **necessary**, not an artefact of
    57	  this route.
    58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the same fact in the
    59	  elementwise form a chart-locus argument can actually use.
    60	-/

   112	variable (C) in
   113	/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**
   114	
   115	This is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single
   116	`g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it
   117	owes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:
   118	
   119	* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` — the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a
   120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
   121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
   122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
   123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
   124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
   125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
   126	
   127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
   128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
   129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
   130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   131	    where
   132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
   133	  W : T.Opens
   134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
   135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
   136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
   137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
   138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
   139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
   140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
   141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
   142	
   143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
   144	
   145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
   146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
   147	
   148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
   149	pullback of presheaves.
   150	
   151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
   152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
   153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
   154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
   155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
   156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
   157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
   158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
   159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
   160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
   162	      φ.app S) D.sq
   163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
   164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
   165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
   166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
   167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
   168	    intro v w hvw
   169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
   170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩

   172	end ChartFibrePresented

   174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
   175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
   176	
   177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
   178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
   179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
   180	each.
   181	
   182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
   183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
   184

   186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;

   195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
   196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),

   202	    inferInstance⟩

   207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
   208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/
   209	
   210	/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**

   219	theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}

    13	ambient maps that the later open-locus restriction must consume:

    16	* `abelDivAffSigma` extends a represented slice map to the ambient big-site presheaf;
    17	* `abelDivAffGenusSigma` specializes the map using the canonical genus representation.

    20	`picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C)`, and `DivRankOneOpen` must be an open of
    21	`divRepAffGenusScheme C`. Its `rankOneAbel` is the restriction of
    22	`abelDivAffGenusSigma`, after applying the corresponding Sigma extension. No placeholder locus,
    23	inverse, representability witness, or endgame theorem is postulated here.

    10	/-!
    11	
    12	# Relatively representable morphisms
    13	
    14	In this file we define and develop basic results about relatively representable morphisms.
    15	
    16	Classically, a morphism `f : F ⟶ G` of presheaves is said to be representable if for any morphism
    17	`g : yoneda.obj X ⟶ G`, there exists a pullback square of the following form
    18	```
    19	  yoneda.obj Y --yoneda.map snd--> yoneda.obj X
    20	      |                                |
    21	     fst                               g
    22	      |                                |
    23	      v                                v
    24	      F ------------ f --------------> G
    25	```
    26	
    27	In this file, we define a notion of relative representability which works with respect to any
    28	functor, and not just `yoneda`. The fact that a morphism `f : F ⟶ G` between presheaves is
    29	representable in the classical case will then be given by `yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f`.
    30	
    31	## Main definitions
    32	
    33	Throughout this file, `F : C ⥤ D` is a functor between categories `C` and `D`.
    34	
    35	* `Functor.relativelyRepresentable`: A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` in `D` is said to be relatively
    36	  representable with respect to `F`, if for any `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, there exists a pullback square
    37	  of the following form
    38	  ```
    39	  F.obj b --F.map snd--> F.obj a
    40	      |                     |
    41	     fst                    g
    42	      |                     |
    43	      v                     v
    44	      X ------- f --------> Y
    45	  ```
    46	
    47	* `MorphismProperty.relative`: Given a morphism property `P` in `C`, a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` in `D`
    48	  satisfies `P.relative F` if it is relatively representable and for any `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, the
    49	  property `P` holds for any represented pullback of `f` by `g`.
    50	
    51	## API
    52	
    53	Given `hf : relativelyRepresentable f`, with `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, we provide:
    54	* `hf.pullback g` which is the object in `C` such that `F.obj (hf.pullback g)` is a
    55	  pullback of `f` and `g`.
    56	* `hf.snd g` is the morphism `hf.pullback g ⟶ F.obj a`
    57	* `hf.fst g` is the morphism `F.obj (hf.pullback g) ⟶ X`
    58	* If `F` is full, and `f` is of type `F.obj c ⟶ G`, we also have `hf.fst' g : hf.pullback g ⟶ X`
    59	  which is the preimage under `F` of `hf.fst g`.
    60	* `hom_ext`, `hom_ext'`, `lift`, `lift'` are variants of the universal property of
    61	  `F.obj (hf.pullback g)`, where as much as possible has been formulated internally to `C`.
    62	  For these theorems we also need that `F` is full and/or faithful.
    63	* `symmetry` and `symmetryIso` are variants of the fact that pullbacks are symmetric for
    64	  representable morphisms, formulated internally to `C`. We assume that `F` is fully faithful here.
    65	
    66	We also provide some basic API for dealing with triple pullbacks, i.e. given
    67	`hf₁ : relativelyRepresentable f₁`, `f₂ : F.obj A₂ ⟶ X` and `f₃ : F.obj A₃ ⟶ X`, we define
    68	`hf₁.pullback₃ f₂ f₃` to be the pullback of `(A₁ ×_X A₂) ×_{A₁} (A₁ ×_X A₃)`. We then develop
    69	some API for working with this object, mirroring the usual API for pullbacks, but where as much
    70	as possible is phrased internally to `C`.
    71	
    72	## Main results
    73	
    74	* `relativelyRepresentable.isMultiplicative`: The class of relatively representable morphisms is
    75	  multiplicative.
    76	* `relativelyRepresentable.isStableUnderBaseChange`: Being relatively representable is stable under
    77	  base change.
    78	* `relativelyRepresentable.of_isIso`: Isomorphisms are relatively representable.
    79	
    80	-/

   288	  id_mem _ := of_isIso F _
   289	  comp_mem {F G H} f g hf hg := fun X h ↦
   290	    ⟨hf.pullback (hg.fst h), hf.snd (hg.fst h) ≫ hg.snd h, hf.fst (hg.fst h),
   291	      by simpa using IsPullback.paste_vert (hf.isPullback (hg.fst h)) (hg.isPullback h)⟩
   292	
   293	instance isStableUnderBaseChange : IsStableUnderBaseChange F.relativelyRepresentable where
   294	  of_isPullback {X Y Y' X' f g f' g'} P₁ hg a h := by
   295	    refine ⟨hg.pullback (h ≫ f), hg.snd (h ≫ f), ?_, ?_⟩
   296	    · apply P₁.lift (hg.fst (h ≫ f)) (F.map (hg.snd (h ≫ f)) ≫ h) (by simpa using hg.w (h ≫ f))
   297	    · apply IsPullback.of_right' (hg.isPullback (h ≫ f)) P₁
   298	
   299	instance respectsIso : RespectsIso F.relativelyRepresentable :=
   300	  (isStableUnderBaseChange F).respectsIso

300	  (isStableUnderBaseChange F).respectsIso
   301	
   302	end Functor.relativelyRepresentable
   303	
   304	namespace MorphismProperty
   305	
   306	open Functor.relativelyRepresentable
   307	
   308	variable {X Y : D} (P : MorphismProperty C)
   309	
   310	/-- Given a morphism property `P` in a category `C`, a functor `F : C ⥤ D` and a morphism
   311	`f : X ⟶ Y` in `D`. Then `f` satisfies the morphism property `P.relative` with respect to `F` iff:
   312	* The morphism is representable with respect to `F`
   313	* For any morphism `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, the property `P` holds for any represented pullback of
   314	  `f` by `g`. -/
   315	def relative : MorphismProperty D :=
   316	  fun X Y f ↦ F.relativelyRepresentable f ∧
   317	    ∀ ⦃a b : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y) (fst : F.obj b ⟶ X) (snd : b ⟶ a)
   318	      (_ : IsPullback fst (F.map snd) f g), P snd
   319	
   320	/-- Given a morphism property `P` in a category `C`, a morphism `f : F ⟶ G` of presheaves in the
   321	category `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` satisfies the morphism property `P.presheaf` iff:
   322	* The morphism is representable.
   323	* For any morphism `g : F.obj a ⟶ G`, the property `P` holds for any represented pullback of
   324	  `f` by `g`.
   325	
   326	This is implemented as a special case of the more general notion of `P.relative`, to the case when
   327	the functor `F` is `yoneda`. -/
   328	abbrev presheaf : MorphismProperty (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) := P.relative yoneda
   329	
   330	variable {P} {F}
   331	
   332	/-- A morphism satisfying `P.relative` is representable. -/
   333	lemma relative.rep {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : P.relative F f) : F.relativelyRepresentable f :=
   334	  hf.1
   335	
   336	lemma relative.property {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : P.relative F f) :
   337	    ∀ ⦃a b : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y) (fst : F.obj b ⟶ X) (snd : b ⟶ a)
   338	    (_ : IsPullback fst (F.map snd) f g), P snd :=
   339	  hf.2
   340	
   341	lemma relative.property_snd {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : P.relative F f) {a : C} (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y) :
   342	    P (hf.rep.snd g) :=
   343	  hf.property g _ _ (hf.rep.isPullback g)
   344	
   345	set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
   346	/-- Given a morphism property `P` which respects isomorphisms, then to show that a morphism
   347	`f : X ⟶ Y` satisfies `P.relative` it suffices to show that:
   348	* The morphism is representable.
   349	* For any morphism `g : F.obj a ⟶ G`, the property `P` holds for *some* represented pullback
   350	  of `f` by `g`. -/
   351	lemma relative.of_exists [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [P.RespectsIso] {f : X ⟶ Y}
   352	    (h₀ : ∀ ⦃a : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y), ∃ (b : C) (fst : F.obj b ⟶ X) (snd : b ⟶ a)
   353	      (_ : IsPullback fst (F.map snd) f g), P snd) : P.relative F f := by
   354	  refine ⟨fun a g ↦ ?_, fun a b g fst snd h ↦ ?_⟩
   355	  all_goals obtain ⟨c, g_fst, g_snd, BC, H⟩ := h₀ g
   356	  · refine ⟨c, g_snd, g_fst, BC⟩
   357	  · refine (P.arrow_mk_iso_iff ?_).2 H
   358	    exact Arrow.isoMk (F.preimageIso (h.isoIsPullback X (F.obj a) BC)) (Iso.refl _)
   359	      (F.map_injective (by simp))
   360	
   361	lemma relative_of_snd [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [P.RespectsIso] {f : X ⟶ Y}
   362	    (hf : F.relativelyRepresentable f) (h : ∀ ⦃a : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y), P (hf.snd g)) :
   363	    P.relative F f :=
   364	  relative.of_exists (fun _ g ↦ ⟨hf.pullback g, hf.fst g, hf.snd g, hf.isPullback g, h g⟩)
   365	
   366	/-- If `P : MorphismProperty C` is stable under base change, `F` is fully faithful and preserves
   367	pullbacks, and `C` has all pullbacks, then for any `f : a ⟶ b` in `C`, `F.map f` satisfies
   368	`P.relative` if `f` satisfies `P`. -/
   369	lemma relative_map [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [HasPullbacks C] [IsStableUnderBaseChange P]
   370	    {a b : C} {f : a ⟶ b} [∀ c (g : c ⟶ b), PreservesLimit (cospan f g) F]
   371	    (hf : P f) : P.relative F (F.map f) := by
   372	  apply relative.of_exists
   373	  intro Y' g
   374	  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := F.map_surjective g
   375	  exact ⟨_, _, _, (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f g).map F, P.pullback_snd _ _ hf⟩
   376	
   377	lemma of_relative_map {a b : C} {f : a ⟶ b} (hf : P.relative F (F.map f)) : P f :=
   378	  hf.property (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) f (IsPullback.id_horiz (F.map f))
   379	
   380	lemma relative_map_iff [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan F]
   381	    [HasPullbacks C] [IsStableUnderBaseChange P] {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} :
   382	    P.relative F (F.map f) ↔ P f :=
   383	  ⟨fun hf ↦ of_relative_map hf, fun hf ↦ relative_map hf⟩
   384	
   385	/-- If `P' : MorphismProperty C` is satisfied whenever `P` is, then also `P'.relative` is
   386	satisfied whenever `P.relative` is. -/
   387	lemma relative_monotone {P' : MorphismProperty C} (h : P ≤ P') :
   388	    P.relative F ≤ P'.relative F := fun _ _ _ hf ↦
   389	  ⟨hf.rep, fun _ _ g fst snd BC ↦ h _ (hf.property g fst snd BC)⟩

1	/-

     6	import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FiniteDimensional.Basic
     7	import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.RightExactness
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Rank-one fibre quotients
    11	
    12	If a vector `1 ⊗ s` is nonzero in a one-dimensional fibre `K ⊗[B] M`, then it spans that
    13	fibre.  Consequently, every surjective image of `M` that kills `s` has zero `K`-fibre.
    14	
    15	The mapped-submodule form is tailored to an ideal `J ≤ B`: if the fibre of `J` has rank one,
    16	`s ∈ J` survives in that fibre, and a quotient map kills `s`, then the image of `J` in the
    17	quotient has zero residue-field fibre.  This is purely right exactness of tensor product;
    18	neither flatness nor finite generation over `B` is needed at this step.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open scoped TensorProduct
    26	
    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    28	
    29	namespace RankOneFibre
    30	
    31	/-- A surjective image has zero field fibre when every source-fibre vector is a scalar multiple
    32	of `1 ⊗ s`, and the image kills `s`.  The spanning hypothesis also covers the zero-fibre case;
    33	no dimension or nonzero-vector assumption is required. -/
    34	theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton
    35	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    36	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    37	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    38	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    39	    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    40	    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
    41	  have hft : Function.Surjective (f.lTensor K) :=
    42	    LinearMap.lTensor_surjective K hf
    43	  have hzero : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, (f.lTensor K) v = 0 := by
    44	    intro v
    45	    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hspan v
    46	    rw [← hc, ← TensorProduct.tmul_eq_smul_one_tmul c s,
    47	      LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, hfs]
    48	    simp
    49	  have hsub : Subsingleton (K ⊗[B] N) := by
    50	    refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
    51	    obtain ⟨x', rfl⟩ := hft x
    52	    obtain ⟨y', rfl⟩ := hft y
    53	    rw [hzero x', hzero y']
    54	  exact (TensorProduct.comm B N K).toEquiv.subsingleton
    55	
    56	/-- A surjective image of a module has zero field fibre if it kills a nonzero vector spanning
    57	the one-dimensional source fibre. -/
    58	theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
    59	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    60	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    61	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    62	    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    63	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    64	    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
    65	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f hf s
    66	  intro v
    67	  exact exists_smul_eq_of_finrank_eq_one hfin hs v
    68	  exact hfs
    69	
    70	/-- If a linear map kills a generator of a one-dimensional source fibre, the fibre of its
    71	range is zero. -/
    72	theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    73	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    74	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    75	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    76	    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    77	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    78	    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
    79	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one f.rangeRestrict
    80	    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hfin hs
    81	  apply Subtype.ext
    82	  exact hfs
    83	
    84	/-- Range specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`. -/
    85	theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
    86	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    87	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    88	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    89	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    90	    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    91	    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
    92	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f.rangeRestrict
    93	    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hspan
    94	  apply Subtype.ext
    95	  exact hfs
    96	
    97	/-- Let `P` be a submodule whose field fibre is one-dimensional.  If `s ∈ P` survives in
    98	that fibre and `f s = 0`, then the fibre of the image `f(P)` is zero.
    99	
   100	For a chart ideal `J` and the quotient map `B → B/(s)`, the conclusion is precisely the
   101	vanishing of the fibre of the image of `J` in `B/(s)`. -/
   102	theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   103	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   104	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
   105	    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
   106	    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] P) = 1)
   107	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
   108	    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
   109	  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
   110	  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   111	    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hfin hs
   112	  simpa using hfs
   113	
   114	/-- Mapped-submodule specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`.
   115	This is useful when the source ideal fibre may itself be zero. -/
   116	theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
   117	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   118	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
   119	    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
   120	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] P, ∃ c : K,
   121	      c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P)) = v) (hfs : f s = 0) :
   122	    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
   123	  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
   124	  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
   125	    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hspan
   126	  simpa using hfs
   127	
   128	/-- Quotienting by a vector that survives and spans a one-dimensional field fibre produces
   129	a quotient with zero field fibre. -/
   130	theorem subsingleton_quotient_span_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   131	    {B K M : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   132	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
   133	    (s : M) (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
   134	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) :
   135	    Subsingleton ((M ⧸ Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)) ⊗[B] K) := by
   136	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
   137	    (Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)).mkQ
   138	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) s hfin hs
   139	  rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
   140	  exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self s
   141	
   142	end RankOneFibre
   143	
   144	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeRedesignRankOneFibre
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeRedesignChartReadIdeal
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Rank-one fibre reduction for the chart colength
    11	
    12	This is the geometric wrapper around `RankOneFibre`: the genuine chart-reading ideal is mapped
    13	to `B/(read s)`, and that image is definitionally `chartIdealColengthModule`.  Thus a pointwise
    14	span statement for the fibre of the ideal immediately gives the desired vanishing of the
    15	colength fibre.  The span statement is allowed to include the zero-fibre case.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    24	open scoped TensorProduct
    25	
    26	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    27	
    28	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    29	
    30	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    31	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    32	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}
    33	
    34	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
    35	
    36	/-- **Pointwise chart-colength fibre vanishing from ideal-fibre span.**  Let `B` be the
    37	pinned-chart section ring, `J` the genuine `B`-ideal generated by the readings of `K`, and
    38	`I = (read s)` for `s ∈ K`.  If every vector of
    39	`κ(p) ⊗[B] J` is a scalar multiple of `1 ⊗ read(s)`, then the image of `J` in `B/I` has
    40	zero `κ(p)`-fibre.  This is the exact single-point input consumed by the `κ(z)` RD-N bridge;
    41	it uses no global base-fibre or flatness inference. -/
    42	theorem subsingleton_chartIdealColengthModule_tensor_residueField_of_ideal_span
    43	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
    44	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) (hsK : s ∈ K)
    45	    (p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
    46	    (hspan : ∀ v : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[
    47	        Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
    48	        (chartReadIdeal K b), ∃ c : p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
    49	          c • ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[
    50	            Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
    51	            (⟨relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s,
    52	              by
    53	                exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩⟩ :
    54	              chartReadIdeal K b)) = v) :
    55	    Subsingleton ((chartIdealColengthModule K b s) ⊗[
    56	      Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    57	  let B : Type u := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
    58	  let I : Ideal B := Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s}
    59	  let P : Submodule B B := chartReadIdeal K b
    60	  let f : B →ₗ[B] (B ⧸ I) := (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ B I).toLinearMap
    61	  have hsP : relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s ∈ P := by
    62	    exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩
    63	  have hfs : f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0 := by
    64	    change Ideal.Quotient.mk I (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0
    65	    exact Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr (Ideal.subset_span (by simp))
    66	  have hzero := RankOneFibre.subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
    67	    P f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) hsP (by
    68	      · intro v
    69	        exact hspan v) (by
    70	      · exact hfs)
    71	  change Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) at hzero
    72	  exact hzero
    73	
    74	end ThetaGeneratorSeed
    75	
    76	end AlgebraicGeometry

 def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=
   IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi)
 
+/-! ## The explicit fibre producer contract -/
+
+/-- A fibre of the rank-one locus over one test class, presented by an open of that test.
+
+The `exists_factor` field is tied to the displayed class `g` and to an arbitrary source value `v`.
+It is the family-level content needed for relative representability; the open immersion itself
+supplies uniqueness of the factor.  Thus this structure cannot be inhabited by an unrelated open
+or by a fieldwise dimension statement. -/
+structure PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
+    {X : Scheme.{u}}
+    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
+      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))) where
+  W : X.Opens
+  fst : yoneda.obj (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
+    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor
+  sq : fst ≫ picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
+  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u})
+    (v : (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor).obj (Opposite.op S))
+    (w : S ⟶ X),
+    (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (Opposite.op S) v =
+      g.app (Opposite.op S) w →
+    ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}),
+      fst.app (Opposite.op S) u = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
+
+namespace PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
+
+variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
+variable {g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
+  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))}
+
+/-- The fibre square supplied by `FibrePresented` is a pullback of presheaves. -/
+theorem isPullback (D : PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
+    IsPullback D.fst (yoneda.map D.W.ι) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g := by
+  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
+  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
+  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
+      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) =>
+      φ.app S) D.sq
+  · rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
+    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp h₂
+  · intro v w hvw
+    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
+    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
+
+end PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
+
+/-- An arbitrary-test fibre producer discharges the relative openness gate. -/
+theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented
+    (D : ∀ (X : Scheme.{u})
+      (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
+        Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))),
+      PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
+    PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi := by
+  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists ?_
+  intro X g
+  let d := D X g
+  exact ⟨d.W, d.fst, d.W.ι, d.isPullback, inferInstance⟩
+
 /-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/

     (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi :=
